what_a_mismatch_means: A dependency of a LIVE forward registration changed content since it was last pinned. That is not automatically a problem — the price-store rewrite moved everything and changed no verdict — but it must not pass unnoticed. Re-verify what the change does to that registration's numbers, append an acknowledgement entry saying what you re-ran and what you found, and only then re-pin. Bumping a baseline without a matching acknowledgement is itself a test failure — since 2026-09-05 that includes bumping it with NO acknowledgement at all, which used to pass: every dependency also carries original_sha256 (the hash it was first pinned to, carried forward verbatim and never rewritten), and the test walks original_sha256 -> ack -> ack -> sha256 and fails on any missing link. Never change a registration's status here; that is the repo owner's decision.

acknowledgements.finding: NO CHANGE to what this registration trades. The commit ADDS build_calibrated_half_spread_frame; default_lazy_prices_config() still builds the raw frame and the live tick path is untouched. Measured for the record: had the frame been switched, best-spec net Sharpe would move 0.5946 -> 0.7456 and turnover cost drag 0.0827 -> 0.0084, with the DEFINITE_NEGATIVE verdict against the 0.95 bar unchanged at every Policy D denominator. Switching it is left as the repo owner's decision precisely because it would move a live track record without moving any fingerprint.

acknowledgements.reverified: THE SWITCH THE PREVIOUS ACKNOWLEDGEMENT (997b5fe) SAID WAS THE REPO OWNER'S DECISION IS NOW MADE. This file's edge_spread cost basis moved from build_edge_half_spread_frame to build_calibrated_half_spread_frame, via a new build_lazy_prices_half_spread_frame that is now the SINGLE builder both run_lazy_prices_screening and the live tick call. Re-verified four ways, not one. (1) 39f7cb5's own unmodified four-scenario runner was re-run end to end on a later day and reproduced all 20 of its reported figures exactly - 4 Sharpes, 12 DSRs, 4 cost drags and the 29/36/36/36/36/0/36 positive-spec counts. (2) Every DSR was re-derived OUTSIDE the pipeline: deflated_sharpe not imported, both formulas typed fresh from that module's own source equations, and every input taken as a PRIMITIVE off the persisted cross_sectional_trial_results rows rather than a row's own stored DSR; all 12 agree to <5e-5 and each hand-derived DSR at N=36 reproduces the persisted dsr field to <1e-12. (3) A fresh three-arm run whose AFTER arm calls THIS FILE'S OWN new builder - the exact function the live tick calls, not a script's inline copy - reproduced the calibrated figures to every digit. (4) config_fingerprint was compared against the LIVE ROW ITSELF rather than recomputed from the code under test. Reports: data/research_runs/lazy_prices_cost_basis_switch_2026-09-05.txt and lazy_prices_borrow_composition_2026-09-05.txt.
acknowledgements.finding: THIS REGISTRATION'S NUMBERS CHANGE FROM THIS COMMIT FORWARD, and the change is the point rather than a side effect. Best-spec net Sharpe 0.5946 -> 0.7456, turnover cost drag 0.0827 -> 0.0084 (9.8x), DSR at N=36/481/857 0.7533/0.5505/0.5083 -> 0.8684/0.7011/0.6609, specs positive 29/36 -> 36/36, pooled median one-way half-spread 24.41bp -> 2.00bp. THE VERDICT IS UNMOVED: DEFINITE_NEGATIVE against the 0.95 bar before and after at every denominator. What moved is that the registration was clearing the 0.50 screening floor by 0.008 at N=857 and now clears it by 0.161. NO STATUS, THRESHOLD OR REGISTRATION FIELD WAS TOUCHED and the forward clock is not reset: cost_model is not in config_identity() and the half-spread frame is data the adapter builds, so config_fingerprint is byte-identical (2dccbf93..., matching the live row) and the drift gate does not fire. Days realized before 2026-09-05 stay priced on the raw frame; nothing persisted was rewritten; the seam is dated in lazy_prices_forward_registration.py's fourth correction. financing_bps_per_year deliberately stays 0.0 - it IS in config_identity, so every candidate rate (17.0 -> e63f283c, the measured 48.16 -> 97d087f7, 215.0 -> f56f3176) re-hashes the fingerprint and parks this row as spec_drift permanently, which is an operational-status change and the repo owner's call. b492394 measured the rate this short leg actually owes at 96.33 bp/yr (17.1% tail names against a 20.0% no-tilt baseline - no borrow-difficulty tilt in either direction), so that decision now has a number instead of a 12.6x bracket; paying it would cost the spec ~0.22 Sharpe and put it below the 0.50 floor.

acknowledgements.reverified: The other half of the same switch: build_lazy_prices_live_panel - THE LIVE TICK'S OWN PANEL BUILDER - stopped calling build_edge_half_spread_frame and now calls the family's build_lazy_prices_half_spread_frame, and translates that builder's refusal (a ValueError when no positive EDGE cell exists to pin a level to) into this module's own documented CrossSectionalPanelUnavailableError, which _process_family already narrows on. THIS FILE IS IN THE SHARED TICK PATH, so it was checked against EVERY registration and not only lazy_prices: all 5 registered families' adapters were resolved in both checkouts and their config_fingerprint, config_identity, n_trials, module_path, universe_rule digest and all 58 specs' spec_fingerprint compared byte for byte. The full test file for the live-panel builders was run (141 passed), and both call sites were checked ADVERSARIALLY: reverting the family builder turns 4 of the new tests red and reverting this file's call site turns the call-site test red, so neither is vacuously green.
acknowledgements.finding: NO OTHER REGISTRATION IS AFFECTED. The fingerprint comparison across the two checkouts found ZERO differences over 5 families and 58 specs, so none can park as spec_drift and no sibling family's identity moved. The diff to this file touches only the lazy_prices adapter's own half-spread line, the error translation around it, and the import block; the crypto, cbop, noa_neutral and short_interest adapters are untouched. Two behaviour changes for lazy_prices alone: its live tick now charges the calibrated basis (see the acknowledgement above for the measured effect), and a panel with no estimable spread is now reported as unbuildable-this-tick and retried instead of surfacing as an unexpected tick failure - the raw builder never needed that because it never refused, it returned an all-NaN frame and fell back silently to the flat cost_bps. NOTE ON THE MECHANISM ITSELF, recorded because it is a real gap rather than a complaint: shared_tick_path entries carry no acknowledgements list in the schema, and unrecorded_baseline_bumps() only walks each registration's OWN dependencies, so a shared-path re-pin is not guarded by test_no_baseline_was_bumped_without_an_acknowledgement the way a per-registration one is. This entry is filed under lazy_prices anyway - it is that adapter's change - and is flagged here so the gap is visible to whoever next moves a shared file.
